newsitem.title: MEXICO: 400 years later, Mexican Indians receive land.
newsitem.headline: 400 years later, Mexican Indians receive land.

text.p: Mexican President Ernesto Zedillo on Friday granted land and money to the Yaqui Indians of northern Sonora state, attempting to resolve a 400-year-old conflict.
The Yaqui claim they have been fighting for their territory ever since Spanish conquistadors arrived four centuries ago.
"Today we are here to comply with promises made many years ago," Zedillo said in the ceremony during which 1.14 million acres were signed over to the Yaqui.
Zedillo also awarded the tribe 40 million pesos ($5.1 million) during the act held at the Yaqui ceremonial grounds.
The money will be placed in a trust to promote farming in the region, benefitting the 32,000 Yaqui people.

"We can't stop just with the lands," Zedillo said, noting a lack of drinking water and health services in this arid land. "I have reached an agreement with the governor (of Sonora state) to create a special programme for potable water this year," he said, pledging another 10 million pesos ($1.28 million).
